messages:
ella_support: Heads-up — customer on Dedicated Private (VPC) reports 401/403 when calling our public inference endpoint through their LB+istio gateway. Works from curl directly to backend, fails when routed via their gateway. Error in app: 403 Forbidden (insufficient_scope).

kevin_infra: Can you paste a minimal repro curl and the failing response body? Also which gateway — AWS ALB, NLB, or their own istio ingress?

ella_support: Repro we have:
```bash
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer eyJ...customer-token...\" \\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n  https://private.example.redwood/v1/generate -d '{\"prompt\": \"hi\"}'
```
Response via gateway: 403 {\"error\": \"insufficient_scope\"}  — token looks valid against hosted API when we hit the Dedicated public endpoint directly.

marta_platform: Interesting — that error usually means our authn/authz layer saw the token but claims/scopes mismatched OR the header was mutated. Does the token show up identical when you capture at the backend?

ella_support: Customer ran tcpdump at pod and at the gateway. At pod: auth header present but truncated (cut off after a slash). At gateway logs the Authorization header absent in some requests. They suspect LB or istio filter strip.

kevin_infra: Two quick suspects: 1) Istio/mTLS ext_authz or JWT policy consuming/removing the header, 2) an ingress proxy (nginx/traefik) configured to sanitize sensitive headers. Some ingress controllers intentionally drop Authorization unless explicitly forwarded.

tom_devx: Also check for header name casing and http/2 -> envoy header translation. Envoy normalizes header names to lowercase; some old proxies expect Authorization with capital A. But more likely a filter.

ella_support: Customer said it's AWS Gateway with an Istio sidecar (Envoy) in front of the pods + a layer of nginx LB. They shared the nginx config snippet.

kevin_infra: Ask for the nginx snippet. If they have `proxy_pass` and not `proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;` then nginx will drop the Auth header.

ella_support: They posted: 
```nginx
location / {
  proxy_pass http://upstream;
  proxy_hide_header Authorization; # accidentally left from debugging
}
```
Customer says it was a copy-paste from older rules.

marta_platform: That would explain drop. But why truncated sometimes and not always? Could be multiple ingress paths — some with proxy_hide_header, some without. Also if ext_authz (external auth service) runs in front of pod, it might take the token to validate and not forward it downstream unless configured to do so (Envoy ext_authz has option `clear_route_cache` etc.).

sre_oncall: Another subtlety: Istio RequestAuthentication + AuthorizationPolicy will validate JWT at the gateway and then inject `x-authenticated-user-claims` or similar while removing the original Authorization header. If downstream expects raw Bearer token, it will fail. Check presence of those injected headers.

ella_support: Customer captured headers at app pod: we see `x-forwarded-authorization` present with full token. Backend expects `Authorization`. Could we recommend a bridge config?

tom_devx: Options: (a) update backend to accept `x-forwarded-authorization` if present, (b) configure envoy/nginx to copy `x-forwarded-authorization` into `Authorization`, or (c) change ext_authz to not remove original header (`filter_enabled`/`with_request_body` options depending on ext_authz impl).

kevin_infra: For Envoy/Istio you can add an EnvoyFilter to rewrite headers: copy `x-forwarded-authorization` -> `authorization`. Example patch:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: EnvoyFilter
metadata:
  name: copy-auth-header
spec:
  workloadSelector:
    labels: { app: inference-backend }
  configPatches:
  - applyTo: HTTP_FILTER
    match:
      context: SIDECAR_INBOUND
    patch:
      operation: INSERT_BEFORE
      value: # lua filter to copy header
        name: envoy.filters.http.lua
        typed_config:
          '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
          inlineCode: >-
            function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
              local xf = request_handle:headers():get('x-forwarded-authorization')
              if xf ~= nil then
                request_handle:headers():add('authorization', xf)
              end
            end
```
This is a rough example — test in staging.

marta_platform: Also check AWS ALB vs NLB behavior. If they terminate TLS and then call internal LB, some header rewrite plugins (WAF) could be removing sensitive headers. Ask if there is CloudFront, WAF, or API Gateway in front.

ella_support: Customer confirms a WAF was present — ModSecurity rule flagged `Authorization` as sensitive and removed it on certain requests (e.g., long tokens with slashes). That explains truncation.

kevin_infra: Okay, so remediation path: 1) Disable that WAF rule for the dedicated endpoint OR whitelist their client IPs, 2) Ensure proxy/nginx has `proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;` on all locations, 3) Add EnvoyFilter or backend logic to accept `x-forwarded-authorization`, 4) Validate token scopes in our logs to ensure correct scope mapping (look for claim `scp` or `scope`).

tom_devx: For short-term customer unblock, suggest a header translation rule at the ingress to copy the forwarded header back to `Authorization` (Lua or envoy). Provide the minimal nginx example: 
```nginx
proxy_set_header Authorization $http_x_forwarded_authorization;
```
or explicitly pass original header if not removed.

ella_support: Sent these suggestions to customer. They're patching nginx to preserve header and will toggle the WAF rule.

marta_platform: One more note — if tokens are OIDC SSO tokens, make sure audience (`aud`) matches our client id for Dedicated. Some org SSO issues show token valid for other audience and get dropped by our auth layer returning insufficient_scope. But given header mutation evidence, that seems secondary.

sre_oncall: I'll add a short diagnostic checklist to run next time:
- curl direct to pod (show headers)
- curl via ingress (show headers)
- capture `x-forwarded-authorization` and `authorization` at both points
- search WAF logs for rule IDs
- check Istio ext_authz and RequestAuthentication configs

deploy-bot: deploy status: infra/patch-auth-header-fix -> staging passed, rollout 50% -> 100% scheduled 2026-03-15T10:30:00Z :rocket:

ella_support: Customer confirmed fix after WAF rule change + nginx config; no more 403s. Closing as resolved but leaving notes for runbook updates. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

marta_platform: Please add runbook entry under eng-platform/docs/runbooks/authz-header-forwarding.md with snippets and the EnvoyFilter example.

kevin_infra: I'll follow up to add test cases to e2e infra: simulate header strip and ensure detection alert fires.

ella_support: Closing thread — will file a short incident summary in support/incidents and link here.
